rounds.text: Bajaj Auto is currently operating under a significant capacity constraint, which paradoxically highlights the strength of its underlying demand [E91, E93]. While the company is currently limited to 50,000 units for EV two-wheelers, it is aggressively expanding total capacity by 25% to reach 9 million units per annum, specifically targeting high-growth segments like EVs and high-end motorcycles [E85, E86, E92]. This growth trajectory is supported by exceptional financial efficiency, with a return on equity of 29.2% and a return on capital employed of 28.2%, both of which significantly outperform sector benchmarks [E12, E13, E9, E10]. The company’s ability to generate over INR 2,300 crores in free cash flow in a single quarter, alongside a massive surplus cash position exceeding INR 21,000 crores, provides a robust foundation for future strategic investments and shareholder returns [E94, E95]. Conceded: the stock trades at a premium price-to-book ratio of 8.59x compared to the sector benchmark of 2.88x [E2, E7], and institutional money flow has turned negative [E45]. Nevertheless, the company’s recent performance remains strong, with compounded sales and profit growth accelerating to 37% and 55% respectively over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21].

Bajaj Auto is currently priced for perfection, trading at a significant premium to its sector with a P/E of 28x versus the benchmark of 26.49x [E6] and a P/B of 8.33x against a sector benchmark of only 2.88x [E7]. This valuation is particularly precarious given that the stock is sitting at 100% of its 52-week range [E5, E50], leaving no margin for error should growth expectations falter. While the company reports strong headline profit growth, the quality of these earnings is questionable, as evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.25x in March 2026, indicating that profits are significantly outpacing actual cash generation [E34]. Furthermore, institutional investors appear to be losing confidence, as evidenced by a negative money flow signal and a reduction in foreign institutional holdings from 14.37% to 9.01% [E43, E45, E71]. Conceded: the company maintains high returns on capital [E10, E12] and has successfully expanded its sales growth in recent periods [E17, E21]. However, the combination of decelerating earnings growth [E69] and the fact that the stock is already trading at its 52-week high suggests that the market has fully priced in the company's future prospects, leaving investors exposed to substantial downside risk [E72, E73].

The bear’s focus on valuation multiples ignores that Bajaj Auto’s superior profitability justifies a premium over the sector; the company delivers an ROE of 29.2% [E13] and an ROCE of 28.2% [E12], figures that dwarf the sector benchmarks of 11.49% and 12.54% respectively [E9, E10]. Conceded: the P/B ratio is higher than the sector average [E7, E63]. However, the bear’s critique of cash generation is outdated, as the most recent data confirms the company generated over INR 2,300 crores of free cash flow in the latest quarter, achieving an 80% cash conversion of profit after tax [E94]. While the bear cites institutional outflow [E43, E71], it fails to mention that domestic institutions have increased their stake by 4.39 percentage points [E44], signaling strong local confidence in the company's trajectory. The claim that growth is decelerating is contradicted by the company’s active 25% capacity expansion [E85, E102] and the fact that sales growth in the trailing twelve months reached 37% [E17], significantly outpacing the 10-year average of 11% [E14]. Finally, the stock’s position at its 52-week high is a reflection of momentum and a 24.9% margin of safety relative to its intrinsic value [E46, E47, E50], rather than a sign of being priced for perfection.

The bull’s reliance on high ROE and ROCE [E12, E13] ignores that these returns are being achieved while the stock trades at a significant premium to its sector, with a P/B of 8.33x against a sector benchmark of 2.88x [E7]. While the bull highlights recent free cash flow [E94], this does not negate the concerning Mar 2026 data showing operating cash flow was only 46% of operating profit [E37] and a cash conversion ratio of just 0.25x [E34]. Conceded: domestic institutions have increased their stake [E44], but this does not invalidate the broader institutional trend of negative money flow [E45] and the notable 5.36 percentage point reduction in foreign institutional holdings [E43]. The bull claims growth is accelerating, yet the company itself admits that motorcycle category growth is expected to slow to 7% to 9% [E81] and that supply chain disruptions have already impaired product availability by 10% to 15% [E98]. Furthermore, the bull’s reliance on a 24.9% margin of safety [E47] is countered by the fact that the stock is currently trading at its 52-week high [E50], leaving no room for error in a market where earnings growth is already flagged as decelerating [E69]. Finally, the massive 2393.4% increase in capital work in progress [E41] and the surge in borrowings to Rs 22,713 Cr [E40] represent significant execution risks that the bull’s optimistic narrative fails to address.

The bear’s focus on the P/B ratio [E7] ignores that Bajaj Auto’s superior operational efficiency, evidenced by an ROE of 29.2% [E13] and ROCE of 28.2% [E12], justifies a premium valuation compared to a sector with significantly lower returns [E8, E9, E10]. While the bear highlights a temporary dip in cash conversion [E34, E37], the company generated over INR 2,300 crores of free cash flow in the most recent quarter, achieving an 80% conversion rate [E94]. Conceded: foreign institutional holdings have decreased [E43] and the stock is at its 52-week high [E50]. However, the bear mischaracterizes the surge in capital work in progress [E41] and borrowings [E40] as mere risk, when management explicitly links these to a 25% capacity expansion [E85] required to overcome the very supply constraints that limited recent sales [E91, E93]. Furthermore, the bear’s claim of decelerating growth [E69] is contradicted by the company’s recent 37% compounded sales growth [E17] and 55% profit growth [E21], which demonstrate that the business is currently outperforming historical trends. Finally, the "negative" institutional flow [E45] is offset by the fact that domestic institutions have aggressively increased their stake by 4.39 percentage points [E44], signaling strong local confidence in the company’s strategic portfolio makeover [E79].

The bull claims superior efficiency justifies the premium valuation, yet it ignores that the stock trades at a P/B of 8.33x against a sector benchmark of only 2.88x [E7], a massive discrepancy that remains a significant valuation risk [E63]. While the bull cites high ROE [E13] and ROCE [E12], it glosses over the fact that the company’s operating margins have remained stagnant at 20% over the last three years [E30], indicating that profitability is not scaling with the company's aggressive growth efforts. Conceded: the company generated strong free cash flow in the most recent quarter [E94], but this does not negate the concerning Mar 2026 data showing operating cash flow was only 46% of operating profit [E37] and cash conversion was a low 0.25x [E34]. The bull justifies the surge in borrowings [E40] and capital work in progress [E41] as necessary for expansion, but it fails to address that these expenditures occur alongside a "negative money flow" signal [E45] and a 5.36 percentage point reduction in foreign institutional holdings [E43]. Finally, the bull points to recent growth [E17, E21] to dismiss concerns of deceleration, yet the evidence explicitly flags "earnings growth decelerating" as a negative screen result [E69]. The company also faces significant operational headwinds, including supply chain disruptions and ransomware attacks that impaired product availability by up to 15% [E97, E98].

evidence.quote: Our aim is to accomplish this exhaustive portfolio makeover within the next 6 weeks.

evidence.fact: The company aims to introduce two new brands in the 125cc segment during the year.
evidence.quote: Further, in the year, we aim to introduce 2 new brands in the 125cc segment to cover the full spectrum of customers in this large segment as well as proposition customers from the 100cc segment to upgrade.

evidence.fact: The management estimates that motorcycle category growth will slow down to 7% to 9% in the near term.
evidence.quote: This is bound to slow down the motorcycle category from its rocking 20% growth in Q4 to we estimate 7% to 9% in the near term.

evidence.fact: The domestic two-wheeler industry registrations grew by 14% year-on-year in Q1.
evidence.quote: The two-wheeler industry turned in a resilient performance as registrations grew by 14% year-on-year in quarter 1, though much lower than the 25% growth of quarter 4, but under the circumstances, a very healthy performance.

evidence.fact: The growth in the two-wheeler industry was driven by EV scooters and the 150cc to 400cc motorcycle segment.
evidence.quote: This growth was driven by EV scooters and the 150cc to 400cc segment of motorcycles.

evidence.fact: The 100cc and 125cc segments were flattish, leading to a 7% growth in the motorcycle industry.
evidence.quote: The 100cc and 125cc segments were flattish, resulting in a motorcycle growth in the industry of 7%.

evidence.fact: The company is expanding its capacity by nearly 25% to progressively reach 9 million units per annum from the current 7 million.
evidence.quote: So, with an eye on the future, we are undertaking an expansion of capacity by almost 25% from the current 7 million units per annum across different businesses to progressively go up to 9 million units per annum.

evidence.fact: The capacity expansion will primarily target EVs, high-end motorcycles, and three-wheelers.
evidence.quote: The key areas to address will be EVs, both two-wheelers and three-wheelers, high-end motorcycles and three-wheelers.

evidence.fact: The company has almost 90 operational joint KTM-Triumph stores to expand reach.
evidence.quote: The rollout of the joint KTM-Triumph stores to expand reach while ensuring store viability is progressing steadily with now almost 90 outlets operational.

evidence.fact: EBITDA margins rose sequentially by 10 basis points to 20.9% despite a hyperinflationary commodity environment.
evidence.quote: EBITDA margins inched up to 20.9%, an improvement of 10 basis points sequentially despite the hyperinflationary commodity environment that I'd spoken about.

evidence.fact: Commodity inflation across the metals complex accelerated through May, impacting the quarter by about 4.5% of revenue.
evidence.quote: Inflation across the metals complex accelerated meaningfully through May, taking the overall inflationary impact for the quarter to about 4.5% of revenue.

evidence.fact: Year-on-year margins improved by 110 basis points, driven by favorable currency movements and improved operating leverage.
evidence.quote: On a year-on-year basis, margins improved by 110 basis points, primarily driven by favourable currency movements and improved operating leverage, which more than offset the adverse cost versus price dynamics.

evidence.fact: Capacity has emerged as a key constraint to the company's growth.
evidence.quote: Capacities have emerged as a key constraint to growth.

evidence.fact: The company's EV two-wheeler capacity is currently limited to 50,000 units.
evidence.quote: So, we are right now at 50,000 units. We are limited at that for EV two-wheelers.

evidence.fact: Sales of certain models in both domestic and international markets were restricted due to capacity issues.
evidence.quote: Capacity issues restricted sales of some models, both in India and overseas.

evidence.fact: The company generated over INR 2,300 crores of free cash flow in the quarter, representing nearly 80% cash conversion of profit after tax.
evidence.quote: We generated over INR2,300 crores of free cash flow during this quarter, almost double that of the same period last year, translating into a cash conversion of almost 80% of profit after tax.

evidence.fact: The company ended the June quarter with surplus cash exceeding INR 21,000 crores.
evidence.quote: The balance sheet continues to remain very healthy with surplus cash in excess of INR21,000 crores at the end of the June quarter, well managed and providing sufficient fuel for future growth investments, strategic opportunities and improved shareholder returns.

evidence.fact: The Board of Directors approved a payout of 100% of the profits made last year, split between a final dividend of INR150 per share and a buyback under the tender route at INR12,000 per share.
evidence.quote: Lastly, the Board of Directors at its meeting earlier today approved a payout of 100% of the profits that we have made last year in recognition of the 100 years milestone of the Bajaj family in India and with Bajaj Auto being the flagship company that started it all. his will be split as follows a final dividend of INR150 per share that will aggregate to INR4,192 crores and the balance of about INR5,633 crores will be towards a buyback under the tender route at a buyback price of INR12,000 per share.

evidence.fact: The quarter was impacted by raw material inflation, supply chain and logistics disruptions, and a ransomware attack.
evidence.quote: It was a tough quarter with RM inflation, supply chain and logistics disruptions as well as a ransomware attack, which you may have read about, but it was defended comprehensively and successfully.

evidence.fact: Supply chain issues and other disruptions reduced product availability by approximately 10% to 15%.
evidence.quote: All of these above issues combined impaired availabilities by about 10% to 15%, more so in exports, high-end bikes and EVs.

evidence.fact: Fuel availability became a major challenge early in the quarter due to the curtailment of industrial LPG supplies.
evidence.quote: To start with, fuel availability became a significant challenge early in the quarter following the curtailment of industrial LPG supplies.
